title: Kangana Ranaut Is Playing a Nurse Who Saved 400 Lives on 26/11. She's Touring India to Find the Real Ones.
excerpt: Before Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata hits theatres on June 12, the actress-turned-MP is honouring healthcare workers city by city. The campaign is more interesting than the film has any right to be.
body:
There is a moment in the trailer for **Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata** where **Kangana Ranaut** — in scrubs, no makeup to speak of, hair pinned back under a surgical cap — stands between a hospital ward full of patients and the sound of gunfire getting closer. She doesn't run. She doesn't scream. She turns to a ward boy half her size and says, barely above a whisper: *"Lock the doors."*

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=8n7bXkykd60</youtube>

It's a small beat. But it's the most convincing thing Kangana has done on screen in years.

https://x.com/KanganaTeam/status/2062870211540525380

**Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata** arrives in cinemas on June 12, and if you haven't heard of it, that's partly the point. This isn't a ₹150 crore tentpole. It's a mid-budget drama written and directed by **Manoj Tapadia**, produced by PEN Studios and Kangana's own Manikarnika Films, about something India knows intimately but rarely sees portrayed from this angle: the 26/11 Mumbai attacks — not through the commandos' eyes, not through the hostages at the Taj, but through the hospital staff who kept nearly 400 people alive while the city fell apart.

> "So many of us make the mistake of underestimating the power of ordinary people capable of extraordinary courage. Medical training can be taught. Bravery cannot." — **Kangana Ranaut**

Kangana plays a staff nurse — not a surgeon, not a hospital director — a nurse who isn't taken particularly seriously at home and is sometimes dismissed by her own patients. When terror strikes, she becomes the person everyone turns to. It's a role that demands less of the firecracker energy Kangana is famous for and more of the stillness she showed in **Queen**. Early word from the special screenings suggests she's delivered.

And it's those screenings that have quietly become the more interesting story.

## The Campaign Nobody Expected

Before the film reaches paying audiences, the **Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata** team has been touring India — not for press junkets, but for private screenings exclusively for healthcare workers. Nurses. Ward boys. Hospital watchmen. Cleaners. Security staff. The people who keep hospitals running through the night and rarely make the papers.

The latest stop was Bhubaneswar, where Kangana and **Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi** personally felicitated frontline workers, presenting them with "Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata" badges. Before that, there were screenings in Mumbai, Delhi, and several smaller cities. At each one, the makers identify local healthcare heroes and honour them publicly.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZPnBeSAorz/

It's a marketing campaign, yes. But it's also one of the more thoughtful promotional strategies Bollywood has seen in a while — particularly from an actress whose public image has been dominated by political controversies and social media feuds for the better part of a decade. There's something genuinely disarming about watching Kangana Ranaut, MP from Mandi, pin a badge on a ward boy in Odisha and mean it.

## The Cast, the Tone, the Odds

The ensemble features **Girija Oak**, **Smita Tambe**, **Amrutha Namdev**, **Esha Dey**, and **Priya Berde** — a cast drawn largely from Marathi cinema, which makes perfect sense for a film set in a Mumbai hospital on that particular night. The focus on ensemble performance over individual stardom is a refreshing choice, and one that suits the material.

The film faces genuinely brutal competition. June 12 also brings **Main Vaapas Aaunga** — Imtiaz Ali's partition love story with Diljit Dosanjh, A.R. Rahman, and Naseeruddin Shah — plus Manoj Bajpayee's **Governor** and the **Lagaan** 25th anniversary re-release. Four other titles sharing a single Friday. Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata is the smallest of the lot, and it knows it.

But sometimes the smaller film is the one that stays with you.

## What NRIs Should Know

The 26/11 connection runs deep in the diaspora — many remember watching the attacks unfold on television in real time, helpless, calling family members who weren't picking up. A film that centres the caregivers who held the line that night speaks to something specific and unresolved. Whether it'll get a wide international release remains to be seen — keep an eye on PEN Studios' distribution announcements in the coming days.

*Bharat Bhhagya Viddhaata arrives in Indian theatres on June 12, 2026.*
